letter_markdown:
# Member Appeal — Request for Reconsideration

**To:** Molina Healthcare — Member Appeals
(Mail to the appeal address printed on my denial letter)

**From:** Cameron Grant, Member ID W314904804

**Date:** [DATE I AM SENDING THIS LETTER]

**RE: Appeal of adverse benefit determination dated 2026-08-08 — Reference number POC-9DD444765E-23652**
**Member:** Cameron Grant | **Member ID:** W314904804
**Denied service:** Rotator cuff repair, CPT 29827
**Plan:** Molina Healthcare (Commercial/ACA), State of Arizona
**Governing policy:** Molina Clinical Policy MCP-404 Shoulder Arthroscopy — https://www.molinahealthcare.com/-/media/Molina/PublicWebsite/PDF/Providers/il/resource/Shoulder-Arthroscopy-Guidelines_MCP_404.pdf

---

## What I am asking for

I am appealing the denial of my shoulder surgery, CPT 29827, which Molina denied on 2026-08-08 on the ground that the requested procedure does not meet the plan's criteria for medical necessity. I am asking Molina to reconsider that decision and approve the procedure. My surgeon, Dr. Okafor (orthopedic surgery), has documented in my records that this surgery is needed.

I am writing because the records already in Molina's hands line up with the plan's own published shoulder arthroscopy policy. Below I quote that policy and then show, point by point, what my chart says.

## The plan's own criteria, and what my records show

Molina Clinical Policy MCP-404 Shoulder Arthroscopy states:

> "Diagnostic arthroscopy may be considered medically necessary when ALL of the following criteria are met:"

The first criterion the policy lists is:

> " Severe, disabling pain and/or a documented loss of shoulder function which interferes with the ability to carry out age appropriate activities of daily living;"

**My records establish this.** My chart documents 24 months of progressive pain in the shoulder that is unrelieved by rest. It documents that I cannot lift my arm above shoulder height and cannot sleep on the affected side. Those are ordinary daily activities — reaching, dressing, sleeping — and my records state plainly that I cannot do them.

The policy also requires:

> "and  Failure of non-surgical management for at least three (3) months in duration including at least two of the following as appropriate:"

**My records establish this as well.** My non-surgical treatment is documented as follows:

- **Supervised physical therapy** focused on rotator cuff strengthening and scapular mechanics, 8 weeks from 2026-05-20 to 2026-07-15, 20 visits completed, recorded in the physical therapy discharge note;
- **NSAIDs for 8 months** with inadequate relief;
- **A corticosteroid injection on 2026-06-08**, which gave only 4 weeks of partial relief.

That is three separate forms of non-surgical management, and the course of that management runs well past the three (3) months the policy itself names — my medication trial alone is documented at eight months, and my pain is documented as progressive over 24 months and unrelieved by rest. Each of these treatments was tried, and each is documented as having failed to relieve my symptoms.

The excerpt above ends in a colon, which means the policy goes on to list the specific non-surgical modalities it counts. I have not been given that list, so I am not going to guess at it. I am asking Molina to identify which modalities it requires and how it scored the three documented in my chart.

The policy also contains this criterion:

> "and  Demonstration of functionally limited range of motion (active or passive) on physical examination as compared to the non-involved side  Failure of non-surgical management for at least three (3) months in duration, including at least two of the following as appropriate:"

**My exam findings are on the record.** My physical examination documents positive provocative testing on the affected side and range of motion limited by pain. My records as I have them do not include a side-to-side comparison measurement. If Molina is relying on that specific element, I ask that it say so in writing, and I will ask Dr. Okafor to supply the measurement rather than have my surgery denied over a documentation item no one has asked for.

My imaging is also part of this file. The MRI of my shoulder dated 2026-06-05 shows a **full-thickness supraspinatus tear measuring 1.8 cm with grade 2 fatty atrophy**. My records also note no active infection, no untreated substance use, BMI 29, and non-smoker.

## A point about which section of the policy applies

The criteria I have been able to review under MCP-404 are organized by procedure — the policy sets out separate criteria sets introduced by language such as:

> "Arthroscopic debridement (limited or extensive) may be considered medically necessary when ALL of the following criteria have been met:"

> "Arthroscopic distal clavicle excision and subacromial decompression/acromioplasty may be considered medically necessary when ALL of the following criteria have been met:"

> "Labral repair/biceps tenodesis) may be considered medically necessary when ALL of the following criteria are met:"

None of the policy text I have been provided sets out a criteria set specific to the rotator cuff repair that was requested for me. Each of the excerpts above ends in a colon and introduces a list of further conditions that was not reproduced in what I received, so I cannot tell which list Molina applied to my request. I want to be straightforward with the reviewer: apart from the sentences I have quoted above, I have not been given the plan's criteria, and I am not going to characterize requirements I have not seen. That is precisely why I am making the request in the next paragraph.

## Request for the criteria Molina applied

Molina holds the criteria it used to deny my surgery, and I am asking for them in writing. My understanding is that the review may have been done using MCG criteria, which I have no way to see on my own. **I am formally requesting the MCG guideline title and criteria applied to my determination**, together with the specific criterion or criteria Molina found unmet in my case, the clinical rationale, and the credentials and specialty of the reviewer who made the decision. If Molina applied MCP-404, I ask that it identify the exact criteria set and the elements it considered unsatisfied. I cannot respond to a requirement that has not been stated to me, and I would like the chance to respond to it.

## Closing request

I am asking Molina to reconsider and overturn the denial dated 2026-08-08, reference number POC-9DD444765E-23652, and to approve CPT 29827 as requested by Dr. Okafor. If Molina maintains the denial, I ask for a written explanation that identifies each criterion found unmet and the records reviewed, along with information about my further appeal rights, including any right to an external or independent review.

**Deadline and submission.** My denial notice states that my appeal must be received within 180 days of the date of the notice, **by 2027-02-04**. I am submitting this appeal within that window and am sending it to the appeal address printed on my denial letter, which I am treating as the authoritative address and the authoritative source for the appeal deadline. If it would help for me to submit this a second way as well — through the member portal at molinahealthcare.com or by calling the Member Services number on my ID card — please let me know and I will do so.

Please contact me at the phone number or address below if anything further is needed. If additional records from Dr. Okafor or my physical therapist would help, I will obtain them — I would simply ask to be told what is missing.

Thank you for taking a fresh look at this.

Sincerely,

**Cameron Grant**
Member ID: W314904804
Address: [MY MAILING ADDRESS]
Phone: [MY PHONE NUMBER]
Email: [MY EMAIL ADDRESS]
Date: [DATE SIGNED]

**Enclosures (as applicable):**
- Copy of denial notice dated 2026-08-08, reference POC-9DD444765E-23652
- MRI report dated 2026-06-05
- Physical therapy discharge note (2026-05-20 to 2026-07-15, 20 visits)
- Office notes from Dr. Okafor, including injection record dated 2026-06-08
- [ANY AUTHORIZATION FORM MY PLAN REQUIRES FOR A REPRESENTATIVE, IF I AM USING ONE]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
